text:
emma: Heads-up — onboarding run for 'sparrow-lite-q3' shows ~2% funcall parse failures, mostly fragmented JSON suffixes from streaming path. attaching quick notes.
raj: ugh. is this streaming-only or also sync endpoint?
emma: sync path looks fine. streaming chunk boundaries seem correlated. sample id 98765 fails every time we reproduce with small batch sizes.
sara: can you paste a failing sample?
emma: sure — raw streaming chunks we captured: ```
{"tool":"search","args":{"q":"how to bake sourdough"}}

{"tool":"open_url","args":{"url":"http://example.com/recipe"}}

]}\n
```
raj: looks like an extra closing bracket fragment merged into next chunk. parser sees `]}\n` with no matching start.
ci-bot: deploy-canary sparrow-lite-q3 v0.3.1 started at 1738889950 — config: stream_chunk_size=512, kv_cache=on
mike: how often do we see this vs normal JSON truncation? numbers?
emma: from 10k canary calls: 198 failures flagged by json-lint adapter. that's 1.98%. failure taxonomy: 60% suffix-only (trailing chars), 30% interleaved-controlchars, 10% payload reordering.
sara: hypothesis: new quantized kernel changed tokenization for certain punctuation, causing chunk splits at different token boundaries.
raj: can we repro offline by forcing tokenization split positions? maybe fuzz the streamer to cut mid-token.
emma: tried forcing splits at byte offsets, reproduced flaky `]}\n` in 90% of fuzzed runs with model v0.3.1 whereas baseline v0.2.9 had 4%.
mike: what about retry logic? do we have a cheap healer — lightweight suffix reassembly + single retry before marking failure?
sara: current retry budget is small for streaming. we could add a streaming-rescue step: if parse fails and last chunk looks like a closing array/object, attempt to append last seen openers from cache and reparse.
raj: risky but seems low-cost. alternative: canonicalize by wrapping stream into an array wrapper at runtime: prepend `[` and append `]` and then try to salvage interior JSON pieces. that handles stray separators.
emma: prototype quick patch: ```python
# salvage wrapper idea
stream = '[' + stream_text.replace('\n\n', ',') + ']'
obj = json.loads(stream)
```
emma: patch reduced failures to 0.6% in canary runs but we need to be careful about false merges.
mike: good improvement. what's QA plan? we should add unit tests for: truncated-suffix, controlchar-insert, and multi-tool interleaving. also add eval comparing semantic correctness after salvage.
sara: +1. also log original raw stream with safe redaction so we can audit when salvage changed semantics.
raj: any perf hit? wrapper string ops are cheap but extra parse attempt doubles CPU for failures only. canary numbers show negligible overall CPU uplift (~0.2%).
ci-bot: canary run 1738889992 -> health: degraded -> failure_rate 1.98% -> post-patch trial 1738890200 -> failure_rate 0.6%
emma: next steps: 1) land salvage-as-fallback in streaming deserializer behind flag 2) add 3 unit tests + 1 integration fuzz job 3) monitor semantic regression on eval set (LLM model eval harness)
mike: SGTM. please add a rollout guard: only enable for q3 quant families and monitor parsed_tool_count delta.
sara: I'll open the PR and add tests. tagging raj for tokenization repro harness.
raj: on it — will push fuzz job and token-split repro later today.
emma: thanks all. cc @mike please watch eval dashboards for next 48h. :eyes:
